QUESTIONS

Useful things to know.

Should we buy software or build it?+

Discovery compares your needs with existing options. A configured product may suit standard workflows; bespoke development can address a specific gap.

Will we receive the source code?+

Source access, ownership, pre-existing components and third-party licences are agreed in the contract.

How is pricing decided?+

Clear requirements can support a scoped project price. Uncertain requirements should begin with discovery and a defined deliverable.

IN MORE DETAIL

Custom software development and website delivery

Custom development is useful when an existing product cannot reasonably support an important business workflow. HeyDock can scope internal applications, customer portals, integrations and websites, beginning with the users and outcomes rather than a list of technologies. Where requirements remain uncertain, discovery should produce a documented specification and implementation options.

Website development includes information architecture, page content, responsive layouts and useful enquiry journeys. A transactional application has additional requirements such as identity, data storage, permissions and operational monitoring. A simple marketing site does not need the same architecture as a multi-user business platform; the stack should fit the functionality and maintenance model.

Software delivery also includes testing, deployment, documentation and ownership decisions. Agree who controls hosting accounts, repositories and domains, which components are licensed, and what support starts after acceptance. Changes to scope should be assessed for impact on cost and timing. Source-code access and intellectual property should be explicit rather than assumed.
